explanation: The gaffer is the chief lighting technician. Their right-hand assistant is called the best boy, and the key grip runs the crew that rigs camera supports.

claims.text: A film's gaffer is the head of the lighting and electrical department.
Sound recording, camera rigging and props are run by other crew members: the sound mixer, the key grip and the props master.
The gaffer's chief assistant is known as the best boy.
The key grip leads the crew that rigs camera supports such as dollies and cranes.

writerNotes: Self-check 9.3. Lint: clean. Claims: every claim listed, risk at or above the C26 floor; the schema's riskReason list has no only or counterintuitive, so such claims carry the nearest listed reason. Datasets: no pinned dataset covers film or TV facts, so every high-risk claim here needs checker evidence from the web. Rival test: Camera rigging is the closest confusion, because grips and gaffers work side by side, but the key grip runs it. Volatility: evergreen; no time words; nothing depends on events after mid-2026. Regional: the work is known worldwide and the options need no single country's local knowledge. Style: Oxford spelling, straight single quotes, plain hyphens, explanation of 26 words. Myths: claims screened against myths.json, no match. Mystery and encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: the gaffer's title is also chief lighting technician, the same job; c3 is marked high only because best boy trips the superlative floor.

evidence.restatement: The gaffer is the chief lighting technician, head of the electrical department.
Sound is the production sound mixer's job, camera supports the key grip's and props the props master's.
The gaffer's first assistant is the best boy (best boy electric).
